name: Entryway Shoe Bench
pitch: A seat plus shoe storage in one flat-pack: slatted shelves, a laser-cut cushion recess, raised so the robot vacuum goes underneath.

stages.title: Cut the sheet(s)
stages.detail: Run the fit-test coupon (slot = tab + 0.1 mm), then cut 1 sheet(s) from the DXFs (CUT layer): 36 m of path, 33 slotted vents in the shelves. Inside-out order, air assist on.

stages.title: Remove char and sand
stages.detail: Brush the char from every cut edge, 120 then 180 grit; ease the seat edge to a 3 mm round-over by hand; sand the vent slots with a folded strip of paper.

stages.title: Dry fit
stages.detail: Stand the SIDES, slide in the 2 SHELF board(s), dividers, RAIL-TOP, then the SEAT. Check tab ends are flush and the case is square; no glue.

stages.title: Pre-finish
stages.detail: Seal all faces now (poly or hardwax oil) - shoes are wet and dirty. Mask the tabs and slots so the glue still bonds.

stages.title: Glue-up (Titebond III)
stages.detail: Glue the dividers into the shelves, then the shelves into SIDE-L, add SIDE-R, RAIL-TOP, and finally seat the SEAT over all top tabs. Clamp across the width; wipe squeeze-out.

stages.title: Screws as clamps
stages.detail: 6 #8 screws (3.0 mm pilots pre-cut): #8 x 1-1/2 in through the side faces into the shelf edges and down through the seat into the side edges (hidden under the frame); then 6 x #8 x 1-1/4 in down through SEAT-RIM into the seat.

stages.title: Cushion frame
stages.detail: Glue and screw SEAT-RIM on the seat (covers the tab ends). The recess holds a cushion up to about 45 mm thick, size = opening printed on sheet 1. Cut the cushion board from the offcut if wanted.

stages.title: Optional cleat / wall hang
stages.detail: For a floating SHOE SHELF version only: Z-bar cleat on the rear face of RAIL-TOP into studs. Do not use as a seat when wall-hung unless every cleat screw is in a stud and the wall half is rated (unverified).

stages.title: Finish, load test, pack
stages.detail: Final coat on the seat, 24 h cure, sit-test with 120 kg, felt pads on the 4 feet, flat-pack in one box with corner guards.

materials.sheet: 18 mm (3/4 in) sanded plywood (basic birch-faced or cabinet ply), 4 x 8 ft x 1; use hardwood ply for a premium version

hardware.item: Seat cushion 1-2 in foam + cover (optional, sold separately)

safety: Seat load rating target 120 kg (265 lb) - UNVERIFIED, load test every design change (sag test at the seat centre).
The center divider(s) carry the seat; do not omit them on benches wider than 800 mm.
Wall-hung (cleat) use: shoe shelf only unless studs and a rated cleat are used.
Not a children's product (no CPSIA testing).

profit.labels: ESTIMATES AND ASSUMPTIONS ONLY - not quotes, not guaranteed, machine time NOT measured on the real machine
profit.assumptions: All dollar figures are planning ESTIMATES / ASSUMPTIONS, not quotes, not guaranteed. Sheet prices: 4x8 ft 18 mm birch plywood $70-110, basic plywood $55-75 (assumption). Machine time uses a sourced RANGE for a 120 W diode on 18 mm ply (low 120 / typical 300 / high 600 mm/min effective, i.e. after multiple passes; see CUT-SPEED-RESEARCH.md); ACMER publishes no 18 mm ply feed rate, so none of it is measured on this machine. Machine wear/electricity $1.70 per machine-hour (assumption). Labor valued at $25/h for the "after labor" line only. Marketplace fees 10% (assumption, e.g. Etsy-style).

machine_time.label: ESTIMATE. Diode = ACMER X1 Ultra 120 W on 18 mm plywood; effective rate = speed / passes. Includes rapid travel between contours and 15 min per sheet of load/focus/unload. Not measured.

commercial_laser.label: ASSUMPTION. Sourced case: 300-600 W CO2 flatbed, single pass at ~600 mm/min (vendor 480-720), 60 m/min rapids, 5 min/sheet, $8/h operating cost. What-if cases: a machine 10x / 20x faster than the diode mid cut+travel time (not sourced for 18 mm ply).

profit.price_band_source: SHORTLIST.md: custom target $140-$300 (estimate); Amazon typical ~$75, Etsy $129-$190 [third-party estimates]
profit.note_machine_time: ESTIMATE: 2.4 h (low-speed case 5.4 h, best case 1.3 h) of machine time per unit for 36 m of cut path in 1 sheet(s) on a 120 W diode, 18 mm plywood. Machine time, not material, is still the limit on profit per hour, but a single test cut on scrap will replace this range with a real number.

unverified: Seat strength and deflection untested (18 mm ply over 1000 mm without dividers would sag about 12 mm at 100 kg by hand calculation).
Machine time is an estimate (120 W diode on 18 mm ply, sourced range, not measured on this machine); cut time and profit/hour depend on it.
Cushion fit depends on the cushion bought.
Composite decking top is a CNC-only variant, not modeled here.
Price band is an estimate from SHORTLIST.md.
